claims.statement: The EUDR covers commodities including wood and derived products such as furniture, and requires relevant operators or traders to establish that products are deforestation-free and legal.
The regulation's due-diligence statement includes country of production and geolocation of relevant plots, showing that structured upstream evidence is operationally important.

contrary_evidence: The Commission page records recent simplification measures and staggered application dates, so workload and timing are not stable assumptions.
Upstream statements and low-risk sourcing may reduce the amount of independent validation some downstream firms will buy.

economics.acquisition_route: Polish furniture and timber clusters through ERP, customs, and compliance channel partners
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A possible path is several hundred SME subscriptions and a reusable supplier graph producing high-margin recurring revenue across Central Europe
economics.founder_time: Initially 10-18 hours per week with legal interpretation provided by external specialists
economics.gross_margin_basis: Expected 70-85% after geospatial validation, secure storage, support, and regulatory review
economics.payback: Unvalidated; ten to twenty onboarding projects plus subscriptions could repay setup
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 5000-20000 PLN onboarding plus 1000-5000 PLN monthly and usage fees
economics.retention_or_repeat: Evidence changes by shipment and supplier; subscriptions persist if reuse reduces repeated collection work

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Each authenticated supplier can serve multiple downstream customers, building a reusable permissioned supply graph and lower marginal onboarding cost
fingerprint.customer: Polish furniture makers, wood importers, exporters, and retailers handling EUDR-relevant products
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Furniture clusters, customs advisers, accounting and ERP partners, trade associations, and supplier-invited onboarding
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Supplier permission capture, geolocation-file checks, evidence versioning, downstream reference delivery, and audit logs without guaranteeing legal compliance
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The operator pays onboarding, a monthly subscription, and optionally a per-statement validation fee
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A covered shipment or product needs defensible upstream evidence and reference data before market placement or export

founder_fit: Strong fit with data pipelines, geospatial validation, and automation
Can start as a narrow Polish B2B product
Does not require inventory or public influence
Permissioned reuse creates a scalable data asset
risks: False supplier evidence could create customer liability
The company could be treated as giving regulated legal advice
Commercially sensitive geolocation data requires strong security
Regulatory simplification could reduce paid workload

structure.control_point: Supplier-authorized access and controlled downstream reuse of geolocation and due-diligence evidence
structure.critical_dependency: Upstream suppliers must provide reliable plot-level data and the service must match evolving EUDR roles and rules

thesis: Obtain authority from timber and furniture suppliers to collect, validate, and reuse their traceability packets for multiple downstream Polish buyers, creating a permissioned evidence graph and recurring compliance utility.
title: EUDR Supplier Evidence Authority
uncertainties: Customer roles and obligations must be mapped after recent amendments
Unknown supplier willingness to grant reuse authority
Unknown willingness to pay versus ERP or consultant alternatives
No evidence packet has been tested end to end
